title: Precision Agreement Service: orchestrate per-batch quant profiles with offline and online accuracy checks
creator: Ava Morgan
description: Design and implement a Precision Agreement Service (PAS) that selects and validates per-request or per-batch quantization profiles (FP16 / FP8 / INT8) at runtime. PAS maintains an 'agreement score' between a candidate quantized kernel's outputs and an FP16 baseline using a compact set of stochastic checks and offline calibration datasets. The goal is to safely increase mixed-precision execution coverage without regressions in application-visible accuracy or reliability. This ticket covers architecture, calibration workflow integration, runtime kernel selection hooks, telemetry surfaces, rollout controls and a canary validation harness.
acceptance_criteria: PAS can receive proposed quant profiles and return a per-batch decision: APPLY / DEFER / FALLBACK
Agreement score is computed within 2ms added wall time per batch in p95 on a 40-token median workload
PAS exposes telemetry: agreement_score, sample_count, output_delta_metrics, chosen_profile, fallback_reason
Offline calibration job integrates with PAS and can upload per-model profile candidates via a versioned artifact
Shadow validation harness runs 10k samples per canary with automated pass/fail based on configurable thresholds
Rollout supports gradual traffic ramp with automatic rollback on accuracy or latency degradation
implementation_notes: Agreement score is a composite metric: token-wise softmax divergence (sampled tokens) + top-k prediction overlap; weights configurable per-model
Maintain a rolling lightweight FIFO reservoir of recent 'golden' FP16 outputs for live accuracy checks to avoid storing full responses
Use a two-level decision flow: fast heuristic (cost/latency) -> PAS scoring -> final kernel selector; ensure decisions are idempotent across retries
Per-batch decisions should consider KV cache compatibility and memory headroom (FP8 may increase transient memory in some kernels)
Calibration artifacts are JSON manifests that reference quant tables; PAS must validate signatures and artifact schema before use
Telemetry tags must include model-version, path (hosted/dedicated/private), region, and customer_tier for later cohort analysis
engineering_tasks: Define PAS gRPC and local API hooks for kernel selector (2d)
Implement agreement scoring module with pluggable metrics (4d)
Integrate offline calibration job output parsing and manifest validation (2d)
Add telemetry events and dashboard panels (2d)
Wire rollout & canary controls into Console rollout APIs (3d)
Performance optimization and p95 latency validation (3d)
test_plan: Unit tests for agreement metrics (edge cases: identical outputs, high variance long tail)
Integration test: end-to-end PAS decision on synthetic workloads (deterministic seed)
Shadow-run validation: dual-inference FP16 vs candidate quant profile, compute agreement distribution
A/B canary: run 5% of traffic through PAS-chosen profiles for 72h, monitor metrics
OOM and safety tests on boundary sequence lengths and batch sizes
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - internal dev: PAS binary behind runtime feature flag, 0 traffic
Phase 1 - shadow validation: 100% shadow-run, no traffic applied, collect 10k samples per model
Phase 2 - canary apply: 1% traffic, monitor agreement and p99 latency for 48h
Phase 3 - ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over successive 48h windows with automatic rollback triggers
Rollback triggers: average agreement_score below threshold, increase in top-99 latency > 10%, customer_error_rate spike
observability_requirements: Dashboards: per-model agreement distribution, latency vs chosen_profile, mem-usage by profile
Alerts: sustained agreement_score drop for a model-version, rapid growth in fallback rate
Tracing: end-to-end trace that annotates kernel selection path and PAS decision id
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy agreement metric on low-entropy prompts -> Mitigation: entropy-aware sampling and higher sample weight for deterministic tokens
Risk: PAS becomes single-point-of-latency -> Mitigation: local cached decisions with TTL and async revalidation
Risk: malicious calibration artifact leads to bad profiles -> Mitigation: artifact signing + structured schema + safety gates before rollout
Risk: memory regressions with FP8 in certain kernels -> Mitigation: preflight memory estimation and conservative default DEFER
notes: Related historical work: early calibration pipeline in ENG-30012 provided the artifacts format used here; reuse where possible
Coordinate with console team to add PAS controls to rollout UI (PM: Priya Shah)
Evaluate integration with Optimize recommendations to propose candidate profiles automatically
